properties.name: MEASURED 2026-10-01 (v0.76.0): the --remote client never reads a 401's WWW-Authenticate or a 403's insufficient_scope, and holds one fixed bearer for its whole life
properties.source: code reading at origin/main a5be4dc (v0.76.0), dev_reflow2 hub session, planning the OAuth client role
properties.statement:
Read at origin/main a5be4dc (v0.76.0), file:line.

THE CREDENTIAL:
- `remote_credential` (main.rs:2861) takes --api-key-env / --api-key-file, else `client_setup::stored_credential` (client_setup.rs:192).
- `KeySource` is None | Keychain | Env (client_setup.rs:46). Its doc comment (:25-26) already reserves "browser sign-in" as another KeySource.
- keyring 4 holds the key as Entry("reflow2", <origin>) (:150-186). client.json (0600) holds where the key is, never the key.

THE SENDING:
- `struct Remote { url, bearer: Option<String>, … }` (proxy.rs:480) holds ONE bearer for the life of the process. Nothing can refresh it.
- `exchange` (mcp_http.rs:255) sends it as Authorization: Bearer (:290).

THE ANSWERS:
- A 401 becomes ServerAnswered{401} with a fixed "key is missing, wrong, expired or revoked … sign in again" (mcp_http.rs:313). THE WWW-Authenticate HEADER IS NEVER READ, so the resource_metadata and scope a server names (api.flo2.io does, 2026-10-01) are dropped.
- A 403 becomes ServerAnswered{403} with the body text (:324). insufficient_scope is not parsed.

The pointer attach (main.rs:2727-2779) and the design watch (upstream.rs:346 credential_for) share the same credential path. A sign-in has to reach all three.
